<!-- pr-reviewer: 5716d312933083d88dce885b7afd1e8e7666e8f6 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The law is sound on its own head, but the PR no longer merges with `main`: it conflicts in code with the horizontal-rotary follow-up to #1020, and that is a design merge, not a mechanical one.

### What looks good
- The geometry is right and conservative: swept radius + 5 mm against `axis_to_table`; fixed fixtures judged by YZ box distance over the work's X span; a box across the line is named, not refused or cleared.
- No new false clear found: a fixed fixture is cleared only when it is wholly beside the work in X (`posting_swing_standing.rs:70`) or farther than r + margin. Facets frame matches the swept work's (fixtures are not aligned by `facets_in`, so both use `world_facets`). Non-finite and empty facets are named (`:55-67`, `:71`).
- `axis_to_table` reads by the same law as `nose_to_axis` (`swing.rs` `work_length`): absent = unstated, garbled/non-positive/on a non-turning part refused by name; included in the machine validity check (`def.rs`).
- The tool half's behaviour is unchanged: the 9 pre-existing `index_swing` tests pass unchanged, so no #1020 verdict flipped. Gating is the same as the tool half (every op of a work-turning A), no new panics/unwrap in the new code, provenance line present, decision file present, no snapshot/golden/process-file/dependency/build.rs changes, `Fixes #1107` and `Changelog:` present.

### Local results (PR head 5716d312; NOT merged with main, see below)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `index_swing` | 13 passed |
| `tormach_fourth_axis` | 12 passed |
| `rotary_verify` | 9 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `machine` | 33 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `microarc_test_part` | 2 passed |
| `rotary_fixtures` | 4 passed |
| `fourth_axis_pose` | 9 passed |
| `camcraft-post --lib` | 16 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: `index_swing_horizontal` and the rest of the quick plan's other app suites on a merged tree (the merge does not build), `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` beyond its `--dry-run` plan. The pinned hit/clear tests are all on the A-about-X microARC rig.

### Requested before merge
1. **Resolve the conflict with `main`** (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`, 5 hunks). Upstream `0722074d` (feat(post): judge the index swing of any work-turning rotary about a level line) replaced `WorkA`/`work_a`/`index_angle`/`swept_radius` with `Verdict`/`verdict`/`index_angle(path, line)`/`swept_radius(world, declared, origin, line)`, now taking a unit `line` and a stacked-rotaries flag. `posting_swing_standing.rs` depends on exactly the items that changed (`WorkA::Judged`, `work_a`, the one-argument `index_angle`, `Swept`/`swept`). Please merge `upstream/main` into the branch (no rebase/force-push) and re-derive the new clause on the new API.
2. **Decide and pin what the standing half does for the cases `main` now judges**: a level line along Y (B about Y; the work's span and the box distances are then over Y, not X, and the YZ-distance code at `:60-75` does not apply as written), a line along another level direction, and stacked rotaries (lines move, the sweep is about the WCS origin). Either judge them with a test of a hit and a clear on each, or name each as not judged in the `SWING_NOT_JUDGED` line. Today the PR's own claim ("what it cannot judge is named, never silent") would be false for a Y-line rotary after the merge, because `work_a`-style gating would silently skip it.
3. Re-run the quick gate on the merged head, including `index_swing_horizontal`, and confirm the #1020/#horizontal verdicts did not move.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` is 1236 lines (already far over 400); this PR adds 13. Fine here, but the standing wiring in `verification_report` could move out when it is next touched.
- The face test judges the full turn for every op of a work-turning A, like the tool half (so a stock radius over ~75 mm on a microARC 4 is refused even for an op that never indexes). That is consistent with the decision file; worth a line in the machine docs for users.
- Pinning coverage for hit and clear on the face and on a low/beside/riser fixture is good; a test of a fixture that only touches the end face of the work in X (`TOUCH_MM`) would pin the edge.

@mkinney: ready for a re-check after the merge of main.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 81e506d2c553414a09d80822f167fdf2f00917a6 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Reviewed at `81e506d2`, trial-merged with `main` at `fe1cb894`. The merge is clean, everything the diff touches passes, clippy is clean, and I found no swing that is now let through and no program that posted before and is now refused for a wrong reason.

### Earlier findings
- **Owner comment (conflict with #818's verdict shape in `posting_index_swing.rs`):** fixed. The branch takes main's `Verdict` / `Nose` / `index_angle(path, line)` / `distance` whole. It only widens their visibility to `pub(super)` and turns `swept_radius` into `swept -> Swept { r, span }`. The tool half reads `.r` exactly as before. Against `main`, `posting.rs` only gains lines, so every post-time refusal on main (#1213, #1191, #1202) is still there.
- **Earlier marker review from the author's own account (read as claims, then checked here):**
  - Y lines, off-axis level lines and stacked rotaries: each is now judged or named as not judged. The code gates on `verdict()`, and three new pins cover it in `index_swing_horizontal`.
  - Re-gate on the merged head: done, and confirmed here (below).

### What looks good
- **One reader for the machine and the origin.** The machine comes from `machine::of_setup(world, op.setup)` (per-setup mounts) and the origin from `wcs_context`. Both match the tool half; nothing is derived a second time.
- **No sampling gap.** The work is judged over the full turn as a cylinder about the line (or, for stacked rotaries, a sphere about the WCS origin), not at sampled poses. A thin clamp therefore cannot be stepped over. Probe: a 1 mm-wide clamp under the bar is struck.
- **"Beside the work" is sound.** A turn about `u` keeps each point's coordinate along `u`, so a fixture whose span along the line misses the work's span cannot be reached. The `(s, z)` box distance in the `(u, u x Z, Z)` frame never overstates the clearance.
- **Frames match.** `facets_in` leaves fixtures unaligned, and the fixed fixtures use `world_facets`, so both sides are in the same frame.
- **Numeric edges.**
  - A work vertex that is not finite makes `r` infinite, so every check strikes. If all work vertices are non-finite there is no span, but the tool half then refuses anyway.
  - Fixture vertices that are not finite are named as not judged.
  - `axis_to_table` is checked by `rate_ok` in the machine validity check and read by the same law as `nose_to_axis`: an absent key means unstated, garbled or non-positive values are refused by name, and inch files are scaled (3.15 in = 80.01 mm).
- **Nothing loosened.** No existing assertion was changed or deleted; the tests are additions only. No goldens, recorded streams or snapshot PNGs change. No process files, build.rs, scripts, `.github` or new dependencies.
- **House rules.** No `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` in the new non-test code. The provenance line and the decision file are present. The body has `Fixes #1107` and a `Changelog:` line, and the subjects are conventional.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Build: `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --no-run` | ok |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: post suites (lib + 3) | ok |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: app suites (lib + 136) | ok, 140 binaries, 1164 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored |
| `index_swing` | 13 passed |
| `index_swing_horizontal` | 13 passed (10 + 3 new; the rework comment said 16) |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `per_op_files` | 9 passed |
| `setup_mounts_post` | 7 passed, 1 ignored |
| `machine_switch` | 6 passed |
| `machine` | 33 passed |
| `machine_key_order` | 2 passed |
| `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| `microarc_test_part` | 2 passed |
| `tormach_fourth_axis` | 12 passed |
| `rotary_verify` | 9 passed |
| `rotary_fixtures` | 4 passed |
| `rotary_letter` | 3 passed |
| `fourth_axis_pose` | 9 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `mcp_edit_machine` | 3 passed |
| camcraft-app lib | 148 passed |
| camcraft-post lib | 38 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Throwaway probes** (local only, not pushed), on the microARC bar:
- A 1 mm-wide fixed clamp whose top is 12 mm under the line is struck, with a clearance of -1.470 mm.
- A fixed block from x = 0.001 past the end face is read as beside the work and cleared, which is correct.
- An op that never indexes (no tilt) is still refused against the face when it is 2 mm inside the margin. This is the full-turn law the decision file states.
- A fixed block through the work across the line is named as not judged by this clause. The program is still refused, by the existing fixture-strike clauses.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **The refusals do not say what to do.** `posting_swing_standing.rs:183` and `:199` name the op, the index, both bodies and the clearance, but give no remedy. The tool half has the same gap. A short tail would help, for example "raise the rotary, use smaller stock, or move <fixture> clear of the swing".
2. **"A0.000 index" on an op that never indexes.** With no index, the text says "the A0.000 index swings the work into...". Something like "a turn of A" would read better there.
3. **Stacked rotaries and the face.** The face is named as not judged. For the rotary bolted to the table, the sphere about the WCS origin against that rotary's own `axis_to_table` would be a sound check. That needs to know which rotary stands on the table, so it could be a follow-up.
4. **Fixed fixture across the line.** It is only named here, so a tailstock-like body that no other clause strikes would post with only a note. This matches the decision file; noting it for the record.
5. **Stale "X span" wording.** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the new paragraph) and the first section of `docs/decisions/1107-swing-work-vs-standing.md` still say "over the work's X span ... in YZ". Since the rework, the span is along the rotary's own line.
6. **`posting.rs` size.** It is 1268 lines on the merged tree, far over the ~400-line guide; this PR adds 13 of them. The standing wiring in `verification_report_by` could move out next time that function is touched.

**Not exercised:**
- A setup whose own machine differs from the document's. The code uses the same per-setup accessor as the tool half, but no test of this was added or run.
- A rotated WCS.
- Stock carried from an earlier setup.
- The release lanes and the GUI.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
